English Literature.question: ১) Who is the author of the novel 'Hans of Iceland'?
English Literature.exp:
Hans of Iceland (original French title: Han d'Islande ) is the first novel written by the French poet and novelist Victor Hugo.
It was published in 1823, when the author was twenty-one years old, it is one of the works that established him as a great master of Romanticism.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ২) Candide, a ___  that is the best-known work by Voltaire.
English Literature.exp:
Candide, a satirical novel published in 1759 that is the best-known work by Voltaire. It is a savage denunciation of metaphysical optimism—as espoused by the German philosopher Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz—that reveals a world of horrors and folly.

Source: britannica

English Literature.question: ৩) "The Stolen Child" is a poem by -
English Literature.exp:
William Butler Yeats (1865 – 1939):
- Irish poet, dramatist, and prose writer, one of the greatest English-language poets of the 20th century.
- He is famous for his use of “Symbolism and Mysticism”.
- He wrote the preamble of Tagore's “Gitanjali” in 1912, which later got the Nobel prize in 1913.
- W.B Yeats got Nobel prize in 1923.
Major Works:
Poems: The Stolen Child, The wild swans at Coole, The Tower, The Winding Stair and Other poems, The Resurrection, The Second Coming, The Cat and the Moon, Byzantium, The Lake Isle of Innisfree, Among School Children, The Lord of Harts, falling of leaves, A prayer for My Daughter, When You Are Old.
Drama: The countess Cathleen, Cathleen in Houlihan.

English Literature.question: ৪) 'Civilization and Its Discontents' is a famous book written by-
English Literature.exp:
Civilization and Its Discontents is a book by Sigmund Freud, the founder of psychoanalysis. It was written in 1929 and first published in German in 1930 as Das Unbehagen in der Kultur.
'Civilization and Its Discontents' may be his most famous and most brilliant work.

English Literature.question: ৫) ‘The Sound and the Fury’ is a novel written by the American author -
English Literature.exp:
William Faulkner(1897-1962):
- American novelist and short-story writer who was awarded the 1949 Nobel Prize for Literature.
- He is best remembered for his novels ‘The Sound and the Fury (1929)’, ‘As I Lay Dying (1930)’, ‘Sanctuary (1931)’, and ‘Absalom, Absalom! (1936)’ etc.

[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৬) What kind of literary work is “The Luncheon” by Somerset Maugham?
English Literature.exp:
William Somerset Maugham (1874 – 1935):
Novelist, Playwright, and story writer.
His Major Works -
Novels: Of Human Bondage, The Sacred Flames, The Razor’s Edge, Cakes and Ale, the Magician, The Moon and Sixpence, Lady Frederick.
Play: The Land of Promise.
Short Stories: The Ant and the Grasshopper, the Luncheon.

Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৭) 'The Wind Among the Reeds' is a book of -
English Literature.exp:
'The Wind Among the Reeds' is a Book written by William Butler Yeats.
In a letter to his publisher, Yeats referred to The Wind Among the Reeds as "a book of short lyrics Irish & personal." It may also be described as a collection of love poems both intense and indirect.

Source: Google books

English Literature.question: ৮) Which of the following is a literary work of Thomas Stearns Eliot?
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Stearns Eliot (1888-1965):
He was a poet, dramatist, literary critic, and editor. His theory of 'objective co-relative' is very famous.
Works:
Prufrock and Other Observations (1917)
“The Waste Land'' (1922)
Poems (1919)
Selected Essays 1917-1932 (1932)
Four Quartets (1942)
Murder in the Cathedral (1935)
The Family Reunion (1939)
The Cocktail Party (1950), published in the Post-modern age.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৯) 'In Memory of W. B. Yeats' is an elegy written by
English Literature.exp:
'In Memory of W. B. Yeats' is an elegy written by Wystan Hugh Auden.
Auden wrote a number of poems about his fellow poets, from A. E. Housman to Edward Lear, but this powerful elegy written in the wake of Yeats’s death in 1939 is his finest commemoration of another poet. As well as being an elegy for the dead poet, ‘In Memory of W. B. Yeats’ is also a meditation on the role and place of poetry in the modern world.

English Literature.question: ১০) 'The Analysis of Mind' is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Bertrand Russell (1872 – 1970): 
Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher, logician, mathematician, history writer, social critic, and political activist. He was awarded the Nobel prize in literature in 1950.

His notable Works:
- Mysticism and Logic,
- The Analysis of Mind,
- History of Western philosophy,
- Authority and Individual.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১১) 'War and Peace' is a famous novel written by -
English Literature.exp:
Leo Tolstoy:
- Russian author, a master of realistic fiction, and one of the world’s greatest novelists. 
- Tolstoy is best known for his two longest works, War and Peace (1865–69) and Anna Karenina (1875–77), which are commonly regarded as among the finest novels ever written. 

Source: britannica

English Literature.question: ১২) The character ‘Robert Jordan’ is taken from the Nobel -
English Literature.option1: ক)  The Old Man and The Sea
English Literature.option4: ঘ) For Whom the Bell Tolls
English Literature.exp:
The character ‘Robert Jordan’ is taken from Ernest Hemingway’s novel 'For Whom the Bell Tolls'.

Ernest Hemingway is an American novelist. He was awarded the Nobel prize in 1954 for literature.
His famous novels are For Whom The Bell Tolls, The Old Man and The Sea, A Farewell to Arms, The Sun Also Rises, Death in the Afternoon, To Have and Have not. 

Source: https://www.britannica.com/

English Literature.question: ১৩) 'All animals are equal but some animals are more equal than others.' This line is taken from the works of -
English Literature.exp:
This is a quotation from George Orwell's allegorical novel Animal Farm.
In it the animals conspire to take control of their farm from humans, establishing 'Animalist' commandments to prevent the reproduction of the oppressive behavior of humans.

English Literature.question: ১৪) 'Kim' is a novel written by -
English Literature.exp:
Kim, novel by Rudyard Kipling, published in 1901. Kim, Kipling’s final and most famous novel, chronicles the adventures of an Irish orphan in India who becomes the disciple of a Tibetan monk while learning espionage from the British secret service.
The book is noteworthy for its nostalgic, colorful depiction of Indian culture, especially the diverse exotica of street life.

Rudyard Kipling, in full Joseph Rudyard Kipling, (born December 30, 1865, Bombay [now Mumbai], India—died January 18, 1936, London, England), English short-story writer, poet, and novelist chiefly remembered for his celebration of British imperialism, his tales and poems of British soldiers in India, and his tales for children.
He received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1907 (first British writer).

His verse collection is - Barrack-Room Ballads.

Source: Encyclopedia Britannica.

English Literature.question: ১৫) 'Leaves of Grass' is a poetry collection by -
English Literature.exp:
Walt Whitman, in full Walter Whitman, (born May 31, 1819, West Hills, Long Island, New York, U.S.—died March 26, 1892, Camden, New Jersey), American poet, journalist, and essayist whose verse collection Leaves of Grass, first published in 1855, is a landmark in the history of American literature. 

Source: britannica

English Literature.question: ১৬) 'Lord Jim: A Tale' is a novel of -
English Literature.exp:
Joseph Conrad was a Polish-British writer regarded as one of the greatest novelists to write in the English language. 

His famous Novels :
- Lord Jim: A Tale,
- The Heart of Darkness
- Under Western Eyes
- Typhoon
- The Rover প্রভৃতি।

(সূত্রঃ ব্রিটানিকা)

English Literature.question: ১৭) What is the literary work of Gabriel Garcia Marquez that falls into magic realism?
English Literature.option1: ক) Raiders of the Lost Ark
English Literature.option2: খ)  One Hundred Years of Solitude
English Literature.exp:
In 1967, Marquez published his most popular novel, One Hundred Years of Solitude, and won international acclaim.
The novel is considered to be the most popular example of magical realism, a style that combines supernatural elements with a realistic narrative.

Source: https://www.hindustantimes.com/

English Literature.question: ১৮) Robert Frost coined the phrase “good fences make good neighbors” in which poem?
English Literature.option3: গ) Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
English Literature.exp:
Robert Frost coined the phrase “good fences make good neighbors” in his 1914 poem “Mending Wall.” While the meaning in the poem may have been slightly more about 'turf protection', it can also be applied to adding value to a home and property. Good fences can offer beauty, privacy, and safety.

His famous poems: Road not Taken, Mending Wall, Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening, Christmas Trees, A Boy’s Will, North of Boston, Nothing Gold Can Stay, After Apple-picking, Home Burial.

English Literature.question: ১৯) Who is not an American litterateur
English Literature.exp:
Ernest Hemingway, Robert Frost, Edgar Ellan Poe are authors and poets of American Literature.
William Butler Yeats is an Irish dramatist, poet, and critic.

Source: LiveMCQ Lecture

English Literature.question: ২০) “There are two tragedies in life. One is to lose your heart's desire. The other is to gain it.” This quote is taken from -
English Literature.exp:
Man and Superman is a famous play which is written by G. B. Shaw.

Man and Superman Quotes:
- “There are two tragedies in life. One is to lose your heart's desire. The other is to gain it.” 
- “There is no love sincerer than the love of food.”
-  “Liberty means responsibility. That is why most men dread it.”
- “Criminals do not die by the hands of the law. They die by the hands of other men.”
- “He who can, does. He who cannot, teaches. ”

Source: https://www.goodreads.com/

English Literature.question: ২১) 'The Cantos' is a collection of poems by
English Literature.exp:
The Cantos, a collection of poems by Ezra Pound(American poet and critic), who began writing these more or less philosophical reveries in 1915.
- The first was published in Poetry magazine in 1917; through the decades, the writing of cantos gradually became Pound’s major poetic occupation, and the last was published in 1968.
-The complete edition of The Cantos (1970) consists of 117 sections.

[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২২) George Bernard Shaw got Nobel Prize in -
English Literature.exp:
The Nobel Prize in Literature 1925 was awarded to George Bernard Shaw "for his work which is marked by both idealism and humanity, its stimulating satire often being infused with a singular poetic beauty."
George Bernard Shaw received his Nobel Prize one year later, in 1926.
Source: Nobelprize.org

English Literature.question: ২৩) Samuel Langhorne Clemens is the real name of -
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Langhorne Clemens is the real name of Mark Twain
and Mary Ann Evans is the real name of George Eliot.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২৪) 'Biff Loman' is an important character of -
English Literature.option2: খ)  The Old Man and the Sea
English Literature.option3: গ) For Whom the Bell Tolls
English Literature.exp:
'Death of a Salesman' is a famous play which is written by Arthur Miller.
• Important character of this play:
- Willy Loman,
- Biff Loman,
- Howard Wagner,
- Linda Loman,
- Happy Loman,
- Charley etc.
Source: Death of a Salesman by Arthur Miller.

English Literature.question: ২৫) D.H. Lawrence’s ‘The Virgin and the Gypsy’ is a -
English Literature.exp:
D.H. Lawrence(1885-1930): In full David Herbert Lawrence. English author of novels, short stories, poems, plays, essays, travel books, and letters.
His novels:
- Sons and Lovers (1913
- The Virgin and the Gypsy
- The Rainbow (1915)
- Women in Love (1920)
- The White Peacock
- Lady Chatterley's Lover
- Aaron’s Rod, Kangaroo etc.
His famous short stories:
- The Rocking Horse Winner
- The Captain Doll, The Labybird
- The Price
- The Fox.
His plays:
- Touch and Go
- The Married Man
His Poems:
- The White Horse
- Birds Beasts and Flowers.

Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica

English Literature.question: ২৬) 'The Birthday Party' is a play of -
English Literature.exp:
The Birthday Party হলো Harold Pinter রচিত একটি নাটক।
তার অন্যান্য নাটকের মধ্যে No Man’s Land, The Room, The Dumb Waiter, The Caretaker ইত্যাদি উল্লেখযোগ্য।

(সূত্রঃ ব্রিটানিকা)

English Literature.question: ২৭) Stella Moore and Miss Adela are an important character of -
English Literature.exp:
• 'A Passage to India' is a famous novel of Edward Morgan Forster.
• Important Characters of this novel:
- Dr Aziz,
- Miss Adela,
- Ronny Hislop,
- Stella Moore,
- Turton,
- Callender,
- Cyril Fielding etc.
Source: A Passage to India by E. M. Forster.

English Literature.question: ২৮) ‘Salt-Water Ballads’ is a literary work by -
English Literature.exp:
John Masefield(1878-1967):
- He is a British poet.
- Best known for his poems of the sea, Salt-Water Ballads(1902, including “Sea Fever” and “Cargoes”), and for his long narrative poems, such as ‘The Everlasting Mercy’ (1911).

His other notable works: Dauber, Reynard the Fox.

[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৯) Toni Morrison won a Pulitzer Prize for fiction for the critically acclaimed novel -
English Literature.exp:
Toni Morrison won a Pulitzer Prize for fiction for the critically acclaimed novel Beloved (1987). She received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1993.
Her other famous novels:
- Song of Solomon
- The Bluest Eye
- Sula
- Home
- A Mercy etc.

Source: Encyclopedia Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৩০) Samuel Beckett is the author of -
English Literature.exp:
Murphy, a novel by Irish writer Samuel Beckett, published in 1938.
The story concerns an Irishman in London who yearns to do nothing more than sit in his rocking chair and daydream.

source: britannica

English Literature.question: ৩১) Which of the following is not Walt Whitman's poem?
English Literature.exp:
Walt Whitman(1819-1892): American poet, journalist, and essayist.
His famous works: A Passage To India (poem), Leaves of Grass, Drum-Taps, O Captain! My Captain!, Songs of Myself etc.

‘The Road not Taken’ is a famous poem of Robert Frost.

[Source: Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৩২) ‘Arms and the Man’ is play by -
English Literature.exp:
‘Arms and the Man’ নাটকটি George Bernard Shaw রচিত। এটি ১৮৯৪ সালে প্রকাশিত।

- George Bernard Shaw (1856 – 1950): Irish Born dramatist. Greatest modern dramatist and called the father of Modern English Drama.
- He is famous for his “drama of ideas”. Awarded Nobel prize in 1925.

His Notable Works:
- The philanderer
- Arms and the Man
- Man and Superman
- Doctor’s Dilemma
- Major Barbara
- Heartbreak House
- The Devil’s Discipline
- The Apple cart
- St. Joan
- Pygmalion
- Caesar and Cleopatra
- You Never Can Tell.

[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৩) ‘April is the cruelest month of all' is taken from the work of -
English Literature.exp:
April is the cruelest month, breeding
Lilacs out of the dead land, mixing
Memory and desire, stirring
Dull roots with spring rain.
Winter kept us warm, covering
Earth in forgetful snow, feeding
A little life with dried tubers.

- The Waste Land by T.S. Elliot.

এখানে, উল্লেখ করা প্রয়োজন Ezra Pound The Waste Land এর খসড়া তৈরিতে/সংক্ষেপণে Elliot -কে সাহায্য করেছিলেন।

English Literature.question: ৩৪) 'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness' is a novel by
English Literature.exp:
'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness' is a novel by Arundhati Roy.
The Ministry of Utmost Happiness takes us on a journey of many years – the story spooling outwards from the cramped neighborhoods of Old Delhi into the burgeoning new metropolis and beyond, to the Valley of Kashmir and the forests of Central India, where war is peace and peace is war, and where, from time to time, ‘normalcy’ is declared.

Source: Goodreads.com

English Literature.question: ৩৫) 'The Island of Doctor Moreau' is a science fiction novel written by -
English Literature.exp:
H.G. Wells(1866-1946):
- In full Herbert George Wells.
- English novelist, journalist, sociologist, and historian best known for such science fiction novels as The Time Machine and The  War of the Worlds and such comic novels as Tono-Bungay and The History of Mr. Polly.
- His other science fiction novels: The Wonderful Visit (1895), The Island of Doctor Moreau (1896), The Invisible Man (1897), The    First Men in the Moon (1901), and The Food of the Gods (1904).
- He also wrote many short stories, which were collected in The Stolen Bacillus (1895), The Plattner Story (1897), and Tales of          Space and Time (1899).

[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৬) ‘Crime and Punishment’ is a novel written by -
English Literature.exp:
Fyodor Dostoyevsky is a Russian Novelist and writer.
His famous novels:
Crime and Punishment,
The Idiot,
The Brothers Karamazov,
Poor Folk,
A Little Hero,
The Eternal,
Notes from Underground.

Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৩৭) ‘Around the World in Eighty Days’ is a travel adventure novel written by -
English Literature.exp:
Around the World in Eighty Days, a travel adventure novel by French author Jules Verne. 

His other famous literary works are:
- Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
- The Adventures of Captain Hatteras
- Journey to the Center of the Earth
- Paris in the Twentieth Century
- From the Earth to the Moon
- In Search of the Castaways

Source: Biography.com

English Literature.question: ৩৮) ‘The Good Earth’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
The Good Earth, a novel by Pearl Buck, was published in 1931. The novel, about peasant life in China in the 1920s, was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for fiction in 1932.
- Pearl S. Buck is an American novelist and writer.
- She was awarded the Nobel prize in 1938 for her rich and truly epic description of peasant life in China. Pearl S. Buck was the first American woman to win the Nobel prize for literature.

Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩৯) Which one is a three-act play by John Millington Synge?
English Literature.option2: খ) A Memory of Two Mondays
English Literature.option3: গ) The Playboy of the Western World
English Literature.exp:
J.M. Synge(1871-1909):
In full John Millington Synge, leading figure in the Irish literary renaissance.
The Playboy of the Western World, comedy in three acts by J.M. Synge, was published and produced in 1907.

[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪০) 'But I have promises to keep and miles to go before I sleep' was written by -
English Literature.exp:
Robert Frost is an American writer. 
One of his famous quotes:
'But I have promises to keep and miles to go before I sleep and miles to go before I sleep.'
This line is taken from his poem 'Stopping by Woods on a snowy evening'.

English Literature.question: ৪১) Who is the author of 'The Trial'?
English Literature.exp:
Franz Kafka, German-language writer of visionary fiction whose works—especially the novel Der Prozess (1925; The Trial) and the story Die Verwandlung (1915; The Metamorphosis)—express the anxieties and alienation felt by many in 20th-century Europe and North America.
His notable works: The Trial, The Castle, Amerika, In the Penal Colony, The Metamorphosis, Meditation, The Judgment, Description of a Struggle, Letter to Father.

Source: Encyclopedia of Britannica.

English Literature.question: ৪২) Gabriel Garcia Marquez is a -
English Literature.exp:
গ্যাব্রিয়েল গার্সিয়া মার্কেজ কলম্বিয়ার একজন বিখ্যাত ঔপন্যাসিক। তাকে বিংশ শতাব্দীর অন্যতম শ্রেষ্ঠ লেখক বিবেচনা করা হয়।
One Hundred Years oF Solitude তার একটি বিখ্যাত উপন্যাস।

(সূত্রঃ ব্রিটানিকা)

English Literature.question: ৪৩) Ernest Hemingway won Nobel Prize for -
English Literature.option1: ক) Old Man and the Sea
English Literature.option3: গ) For Whom the Bell Tolls
English Literature.exp:
The Nobel Prize in Literature 1954 was awarded to Ernest Miller Hemingway "for his mastery of the art of narrative, most recently demonstrated in The Old Man and the Sea, and for the influence that he has exerted on contemporary style."

Source: nobelprize.org

English Literature.question: ৪৪) 'Ulysses’ is a novel written by ___ James Joyce.
English Literature.exp:
Ulysses, a novel by Irish writer James Joyce, was first published in book form in 1922.
The novel is constructed as a modern parallel to Homer’s Odyssey.

[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৫) 'Marlow' is a character from -
English Literature.exp:
Heart of Darkness, a novella by Joseph Conrad that was first published in 1899 in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine and then in Conrad’s Youth.
Some characters from this novella are - Marlow, Kurtz, Manager.

Source: britannica and CliffsNotes

English Literature.question: ৪৬) Who is known as the father of detective stories?
English Literature.exp:
- Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer, editor, and literary critic.
- He is generally considered the inventor of the detective fiction genre.
- Edgar Allan Poe created this new literary genre when he wrote ‘The Murders in the Rue Morgue’.
- Nearly forty-five years after Poe’s death, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle popularized the detective story when he created Sherlock Holmes.

English Literature.question: ৪৭) Which one is an autobiographical history of the war by Winston Churchill?
English Literature.exp:
Winston Churchill, British statesman, orator, and author who as prime minister (1940–45, 1951–55) rallied the British people during World War II and led his country from the brink of defeat to victory.

Notable Works of Winston Churchill:
“The World Crisis”
“The Story of the Malakand Field Force”
“Marlborough: His Life and Times”
“Lord Randolph Churchill”
“The River War”

“The World Crisis” by him is an autobiographical history of the war.

Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৪৮) Who wrote 'The Ant and the Grasshopper'?
English Literature.exp:
William Somerset Maugham (1874 – 1935):
Novelist, Playwright, and story writer.
His Major Works -
Novels: Of Human Bondage, The Sacred Flames, The Razor’s Edge, Cakes and Ale, the Magician, The Moon and Sixpence, Lady Frederick.
Play: The Land of Promise.
Short Stories: The Ant and the Grasshopper, the Luncheon.

Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

English Literature.question: ৪৯) The literary work 'Four Quarters' is a poem by -
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Stearns Eliot(1888-1965):
-He is an American Born British poet Dramatist and Social Critic.
-He is famous for his Theory of Objective correlatives.
-He is best known as a leader of the Modernist movement in poetry.
Famous poem of T.S. Eliot are- The Waste Land, Gerontion, Journey to the Magi, Ash Wednesday, Four Quarters, The Hollow Man, Portrait of a Lady.
His famous drama are Murder in Cathedral, The Family Reunion, The Cocktail Party, The Elder Statement.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.]

English Literature.question: ৫০) "Prejudices are what fools use for reason." is said by -
English Literature.exp:
Famous quotation of Voltaire:
- If God did not exist, it would be necessary to invent him.
- Prejudices are what fools use for reason.
